conclusion: The misstatement is superannuation guarantee of AUD 4,261.20 not accrued at 30 September 2026: 12% of the wages for the period and the wages accrued to the period end; it arose in the current period. It is factual: the rate is set by law and the wages come from the payroll register, so there is no doubt about the amount. There is no indication of fraud: no superannuation was recorded for the first quarter of payroll, an omission of a period-end accrual.

reasoning_chain.text: Wages and salaries (477) total AUD 33,500.00 for the period, the five fortnightly pay runs from 2 August to 27 September 2026.

The payroll register shows three full-time employees who started on 20 July 2026, paid AUD 6,700.00 in total per 14-day pay period; the last pay period ended on 27 September 2026 and the next pay day is 11 October 2026.

A factual misstatement is one about which there is no doubt; a judgemental misstatement arises from management judgements, such as accounting estimates, that the auditor considers unreasonable (ASA 450 para A6).
When the auditor identifies a misstatement, the auditor evaluates whether it is indicative of fraud (ASA 240 para 36).
The superannuation guarantee follows from the statutory rate and the recorded wages, so the misstatement is factual and arose in the current period.
The omission of the first quarterly accrual of a new payroll gives no indication of fraud.

counter_argument: Evidence that the contributions were paid and recorded in another account would remove the misstatement.
